Main.sentence: Punahou School (known as Oahu College until 1934) is a private, ___E:co-educational U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Co-educational)___ , ___E:college preparatory school U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_preparatory_school)___ in ___E:Honolulu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honolulu)___ , ___E:Hawaii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii)___ .
More than 3,700 students attend the school from ___E:kindergarten U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kindergarten)___ through ___E:12th grade U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twelfth_grade)___ .
The school was established by ___E:Protestant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestantism)___ missionaries in 1841.
From 1853 to 1934, the school was known as ___E:Oahu College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oahu_College)___ .
Punahou has educated members of the Hawaiian royal family, but is not to be confused with the ___E:Royal School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_School_(Hawaii))___ .
During World War II, the ___E:U.S. Army Corps of Engineers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Army_Corps_of_Engineers)___ commandeered much of the Punahou campus.

Castle Hall, formerly the girls' dormitory when Punahou had boarding students, was used as a command center, buildings were connected with tunnels, athletic fields were used as parking lots, and the library was cleared to become sleeping quarters and an officer's mess. The ___E:cereus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hylocereus_undatus)___ hedge on the campus lava rock wall was topped with barbed wire. Punahou students volunteered in hospitals and raised enough in war bonds to purchase two bombers and a fighter (among other airplanes), which were named after alumni who had fallen in service.
On August 7, 1972, the campus was added to the ___E:National Register of Historic Places listings in Oahu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places_listings_in_Oahu)___ .
Many traditional events take place on campus.
On the first Friday and Saturday of each February, the junior class hosts the Punahou Carnival.
Proceeds from the carnival contribute to the Financial Aid program.
The event is an entertainment highlight each year in Honolulu.
All 9-11th grade students are required to work at least one 3-hour shift per carnival, and all students are let out of class early on Friday (typically before lunch) to enjoy the Carnival.

The ___E:Holoku U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holoku)___ Pageant is an annual celebration of the Hawaiian culture and arts. Students perform Hawaiian dances in traditional costumes, from the lovely ___E:hula U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hula)___ to the intimidating ___E:haka U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haka)___ .
The annual Sustainability Fair began in 2007 and included on-campus conservation challenges and off-campus coastline preservation.
On Rice Field, classes set up canopies to showcase sustainable undertakings and projects, often including local produce sales and informational handouts.

To celebrate the school's ___E:homecoming U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homecoming)___ , students, faculty, and teachers surround a 20-foot letter P, and ignite it at dusk. This event, the "Flaming P", is preceded by a spirit week, where students dress and parade creatively.
Seniors write and perform a Variety Show. This play involves most of the class, over 300 students.

Seniors also have ___E:prom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prom)___ at the ___E:Sheraton Waikiki Hotel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheraton_Waikiki_Hotel)___ , Skip Day at the Kikila Estate and Pounders Beach, and senior lunch.

With each student attired in either a blue blazer or a formal white Hawaiian dress, senior year ends with ___E:baccalaureate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor%27s_degree)___ ceremonies at Central Union Church, and ___E:commencement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graduation)___ at ___E:Stan Sheriff Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stan_Sheriff_Center)___  (since 2018).
Graduates who started Punahou in kindergarten are members of the Thirteen Plus Club.
In June, the school hosts an Alumni ___E:Luau U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luau)___ on campus that the newly graduated class can enjoy with other alumni.
The annual luau also functions as a major fundraising event for the school.

Throughout most of the school's history, elementary schoolchildren have been allowed to attend in ___E:bare feet U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barefoot)___ . ___E:Aloha shirts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aloha_shirt)___ were once restricted to Fridays, but dress codes were relaxed considerably during the 1970s.
G-Term is an effort for students to explore extracurricular opportunities over the week after students return from winter break.
Students can choose from on- and off-island classes.
All schools in ___E:Honolulu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honolulu)___ city (public and private) have an urban residential location.

Nearby buildings include apartment buildings, private houses, a retirement home, a Catholic school ( ___E:Maryknoll School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryknoll_School)___ ), several small churches, and two hospitals.

Punahou shares the entrance to ___E:Manoa Valley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manoa_Valley)___ with the ___E:University of Hawaii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Hawaii)___ main campus and a few other schools such as ___E:Mid-Pacific Institute U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mid-Pacific_Institute)___ .

Punahou students are a few minutes away from the trail to ___E:Manoa Falls U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manoa_Falls)___ , the beaches at ___E:Ala Moana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ala_Moana)___ and ___E:Waikiki U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waikiki)___ , ___E:downtown Honolulu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Honolulu)___ , ___E:Lyon Arboretum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyon_Arboretum)___ , and the ___E:National Memorial Cemetery of the Pacific U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Memorial_Cemetery_of_the_Pacific)___ .

Punahou's location provides many opportunities for off-campus learning: field trip destinations for middle school students have included the ___E:Bishop Museum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bishop_Museum)___ , ___E:Waikiki Aquarium U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waikiki_Aquarium)___ , ___E:Waikiki Shell U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waikiki_Shell)___ , ___E:Waikiki Natatorium War Memorial U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waikiki_Natatorium_War_Memorial)___ , ___E:Kawaiahaʻo Church U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kawaiaha%CA%BBo_Church)___ , ___E:Sea Life Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Life_Park_Hawaii)___ , ___E:USS Arizona Memorial U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Arizona_Memorial)___ , ___E:Valley of the Temples Memorial Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valley_of_the_Temples_Memorial_Park)___ , ___E:Fort Ruger U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Ruger)___ at ___E:Diamond Head U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diamond_Head,_Hawaii)___ , ___E:Hanauma Bay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanauma_Bay)___ , ___E:Honolulu Museum of Art U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honolulu_Museum_of_Art)___ , ___E:Honolulu Zoo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honolulu_Zoo)___ , ___E:Iolani Palace U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iolani_Palace)___ , ___E:Hawaii State Capitol U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii_State_Capitol)___ , and the beaches on Oahu's ___E:North Shore U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Shore_(Oahu))___ .

Clubs and classes often organize trips to neighboring islands, especially to ___E:Hawaii Volcanoes National Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii_Volcanoes_National_Park)___ and the ___E:Kohala Coast U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kohala,_Hawaii)___ on the ___E:Big Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii_(island))___ .

Tuition was $30,480 for the 2023–24 school year,  not including student activity fees. Tuition does not cover the entire cost of educating a student, and the school's endowment makes up the difference.

Punahou reported its endowment at $239 million in 2014.  Although these figures are high among mainland U.S. private schools, Honolulu's ___E:Iolani School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iolani_School)___ has a comparable endowment (twice the endowment per pupil), and ___E:Kamehameha Schools U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamehameha_Schools)___ has a $5 to $9 billion endowment (30 times the endowment per pupil) with a larger physical plant.  ___E:Maui U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maui)___ has ___E:Seabury Hall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seabury_Hall)___ , which has twice the endowment per pupil.
In the class of 2015, three graduates went to Harvard, three to Princeton, and two to Yale, with 22 total at Ivy League schools.
Seven attended Swarthmore, Wellesley, Amherst, Tufts, or Vassar.
Four attended Stanford, two Berkeley, four Massachusetts Institute of Technology, 16 Boston University, and 12 New York University, with 23 total at University Athletic Association schools.

Students in that class also chose Texas Christian, Notre Dame, Vanderbilt, Villanova, Rensselaer Polytechnic, Rochester Institute of Technology, Michigan, Northeastern, Boston College, Olin Engineering, Norwich Military College, NYU Shanghai, Erasmus/Rotterdam, Yonsei/S. Korea, Waseda/Japan, and Edinburgh/UK. Six were selected for study and training at US military academies.

Schools throughout California, Washington, Oregon, Colorado, Utah, Arizona, and Nevada are also popular among graduates, and many students choose to attend local schools like the ___E:University of Hawaii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Hawaii)___ and ___E:Chaminade U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaminade_University_of_Honolulu)___ .
The class of 2012 had 30 of Hawaii's 70 ___E:National Merit Semifinalists U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Merit_Semifinalists)___ .
The class of 2013 had 20 semifinalists, and five of the state's ten ___E:National Merit Scholars U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Merit_Scholars)___ .

Punahou's 33 ___E:Presidential Scholars U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_Scholars_Program)___ were graduates of the classes of '64, '66, '70, '71, '75, '78 (two), '79, '82, '84 (two members), '85, '86 (two), '91, '92 (two), '93, '95, '96, '98, '01, '02, '04 (three), '05, '06, '08, '11, '16 (two), '17, and '21.
In 2006, it was ranked the greenest school in America.
In 2017, Punahou's sports program was ranked second nationally in the MaxPreps Cup standings.
Punahou's student body is diverse, with student selection based on both academic and non-academic considerations.

The school is a founding member of the ___E:Mastery Transcript Consortium U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mastery_Transcript_Consortium)___ , and uses a ___E:competency-based learning U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Competency-based_learning)___ framework in some courses.

A recent study of the class of 1979  showed that 15 had a PhD, 22 had an MD, 39 had a JD, 18 had the MBA, 10 had the DDS, DMD, DVM, or ND (about one quarter of the class reaching terminal degrees). 4 were officers in the US armed services. 12 had degrees from Harvard, Yale, or Princeton, 14 from Stanford, 17 from UC Berkeley, and 26 total from Ivy League schools.
About 5,000 faculty, students, and staff work in 44 buildings on 76 acres.

The Robert Thurston Memorial Chapel on campus was building designed and built in 1966 by architect ___E:Vladimir Ossipoff U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Ossipoff)___ and feature textile screens made by local artist ___E:Ruthadell Anderson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruthadell_Anderson)___ .
The school is built over a ___E:natural spring U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spring_(hydrology))___ .
Thurston Chapel's wall meets at a pond formed by the spring and features a low hung ___E:stained glass U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stained_glass)___ .

Before plans were made for a new middle school complex, ___E:America Online U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America_Online)___ founder and alumnus ___E:Steve Case U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Case)___ ('76) donated $10 million.
This led to construction of a new middle school for grades six through eight, Case Middle School, named for Case's parents.

The project earned a ___E:Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leadership_in_Energy_and_Environmental_Design)___ Gold certification   and a Project of the Year award in ___E:Hawaiian Electric Company U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaiian_Electric_Company)___ 's Energy Efficiency Awards.
Case Middle School consists of nine buildings with a total cost of roughly $50 million, made possible solely through donations.
In late 2010 a new five-building indoor/outdoor section of campus opened for Punahou's youngest students.
It was constructed and operated with sustainable living as a principal goal, and the curriculum has a focus on sustainability.
With solar energy, efficient landscaping, rain catchment and ecofriendly materials, the complex received a platinum rating from the U.S.
Green Building Council.
Teachers are encouraged to personalize their classroom spaces,  and each of the 12 rooms has its own outdoor area that is one-third the size of the interior space to which it is attached.
The total cost was $26 million.

Individual buildings are named the Mountain House, Forest House, and City House, and historic Wilcox Hall retains its traditional name. Board of Trustees member and ___E:eBay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EBay)___ founder ___E:Pierre Omidyar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_Omidyar)___ ('84) donated $6 million to the project.
Punahou's athletics program is the most successful in Hawaii.
It has won more state championships than any other high school in the nation.
In 2008 and in 2009, Sports Illustrated ranked Punahou's sports program the best in the country.

Punahou football plays the second half of its season at the ___E:Aloha Stadium U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aloha_Stadium)___ (where the ___E:Pro Bowl U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Bowl)___ and ___E:Aloha Bowl U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aloha_Bowl)___ were played).
In fall 2014, the varsity football team ranked as high as 15th in the nation.
Athletic facilities include the Olympic-size Waterhouse Pool, a football field, a baseball diamond, two softball diamonds, and an eight-lane track.

The school also has a fieldhouse for competitive athletics, an open-air weightlifting facility, a gymnasium for physical education and intramural sports, and a tennis center with eight hard surface courts.
Rocky Hill has been used as a live firing range for ___E:JROTC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JROTC)___ and competitive target sports.
Air riflery uses an indoor firing range.
Students need two athletic credits to graduate, which is a total of four semesters.
They can earn these credits through P.E. and ILH sports.

Students compete in 22 sports, including ___E:air riflery U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_riflery)___ , ___E:baseball U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baseball)___ , ___E:basketball U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball)___ , ___E:bowling U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bowling)___ , ___E:canoe paddling U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canoe_paddling)___ , ___E:cross country U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_country_running)___ , ___E:cheerleading U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheerleading)___ , ___E:football U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football)___ , ___E:golf U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golf)___ , ___E:gymnastics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gymnastics)___ , ___E:judo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judo)___ , ___E:kayaking U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kayaking)___ , ___E:riflery U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riflery)___ , ___E:sailing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sailing_(sport))___ , ___E:soccer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soccer)___ , ___E:softball U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Softball)___ , ___E:swimming U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_(sport))___ and ___E:diving U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diving_(sport))___ , ___E:tennis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennis)___ , ___E:track and field U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Track_and_field)___ , ___E:volleyball U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volleyball)___ , ___E:water polo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_polo)___ , and ___E:wrestling U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scholastic_wrestling)___ .
Punahou has approximately 120 sports teams.
The school is a member of the ___E:Interscholastic League of Honolulu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interscholastic_League_of_Honolulu)___ .
Punahou teams earned 20 championships in 2009–10, out of about 30 varsity it teams fielded.
Punahou requires all students (K-12) to attend ___E:chapel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chapel)___ once a week,  where each homeroom is assigned its own seating and attendance is taken.
In addition, students attend a mandatory weekly assembly to listen to announcements or watch student performances.
___E:115801 Punahou U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/115801_Punahou)___ is a ___E:minor planet U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minor_planet)___ named in the school's honor.

In April 2020, several former Punahou girls' basketball players filed a lawsuit over alleged abuse committed by their former coach Dwayne Yuen.   Days later, the school disclosed additional sexual assault allegations dating back to the 1970s involving a former faculty member and baseball coach.

In January 2021, the school ___E:terminated the employment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Termination_of_employment)___ of a high school teacher based on ___E:allegations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allegation)___ of sexual misconduct involving a former student.

The teacher had been suspended from teaching and banned from campus since late November 2020 pending an internal investigation, which he did not cooperate with. The investigation found that the allegations were credible.

Punahou has produced many leaders in the government of ___E:Hawaii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii)___ . ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ ('79) was the 44th President of the United States.
He attended Punahou from 5th grade until graduation.

___E:Sanford Dole U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanford_Dole)___ (1864) was President of the brief ___E:Republic of Hawaii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Hawaii)___ , then ___E:Governor of Hawaii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Hawaii)___ . ___E:Walter Frear U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Frear)___ (1881) and ___E:Lawrence M. Judd U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_M._Judd)___ (1905) were also Governors.
Democratic Lt. Governor ___E:Brian Schatz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Schatz)___ ('90) was appointed U.S.
Senator to complete ___E:Daniel Inouye U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Inouye)___ 's final term. Republican U.S.

Senator Connecticut ___E:Hiram Bingham III U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiram_Bingham_III)___ (1892) was also elected governor of Connecticut. ___E:Otis Pike U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otis_Pike)___ ('39*), Democratic Congressman from New York, chaired the ___E:Pike Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pike_Committee)___ investigating ___E:Richard Nixon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon)___ .

Republican ___E:Charles Djou U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Djou)___ ('88) recently finished ___E:Neil Abercrombie U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Abercrombie)___ 's term as Congressman from Hawaii.
At least three other Punahou graduates have represented Hawaii in the U.S.
House.

President ___E:Dwight Eisenhower U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_Eisenhower)___ appointed Judge ___E:Elbert Tuttle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elbert_Tuttle)___ (1914) to lead the federal court that desegregated the South (the ___E:Fifth Circuit Four U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifth_Circuit_Four)___ ). ___E:HEW U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Health,_Education,_and_Welfare)___ Secretary ___E:John W. Gardner U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_W._Gardner)___ ('29*) was President ___E:Lyndon Johnson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_Johnson)___ 's architect of the ___E:Great Society U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Society)___ .
Tuttle and Gardner were awarded the ___E:Presidential Medal of Freedom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_Medal_of_Freedom)___ .

___E:Sun Yat-Sen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Yat-Sen)___ , the ___E:Founding Father U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Founding_Father)___ of the ___E:Republic of China U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_China_(1912%E2%80%931949))___ (esteemed by ___E:Taiwan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiwan)___ as well as pre- and post-communist mainland China), attended Punahou ( Oahu College ) for a semester of study after graduating from ___E:Iolani School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iolani_School)___ .
___E:Pierre Omidyar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_Omidyar)___ , billionaire founder of ebay, founded The Intercept and other public-affairs websites.

Alexander Cartwright III (1869) and his classmates were some of the earliest players of baseball ( ___E:Alexander Cartwright U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Cartwright)___ , Jr., the official inventor of the game, spent the end of his life in Honolulu).
The school claims at least one former pitcher and a former first baseman in Major League Baseball, and nine minor leaguers.
All-American Glenn Goya ('73) was an NCAA batting title winner.

Oʻahu A
Oʻahu a, Oʻahu a Punahou, our Punahou; Mau a Mau, oh mau a mau, Punahou, our Punahou.
Throughout the years we've shown our light, We glory in Oʻahu's might; The Buff and Blue's a glorious sight, Punahou, our Punahou.
The song is sung to the tune of Maryland, My Maryland , also known as "O Tannenbaum".
The lyrics are taken from a poem, "Oahu Wa," by then student Wilhelm Albert Gartner (1902).
